justifications.layering: Data moves cleanly from source to staging (one model per raw table, `clean_text`/`parse_date`/`dedupe` macros, no joins) to intermediate (`int_seasons`, `int_driver_ids`, `int_pit_stops_enriched`) to marts, all through ref/source. There are some leaks, though: `mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql` repeats the ≤60 s service-stop filter and the constructor join that `int_pit_stops_enriched.sql` already does, and marts like `mart_driver_standings_by_round.sql` and `fct_results.sql` join staging models directly instead of reusing a shared intermediate.
justifications.naming: Model names follow `stg_<source>__<entity>`, `int_`, `fct_`/`dim_`/`mart_`, YAML files follow `_<dir>__models.yml` / `__sources.yml` / `__unit_tests.yml`, and columns use unit suffixes like `_ms` and `_pct`. Two things cost a point: `fct_`, `dim_` and `mart_` are mixed inside the same mart folders (for example `dim_driver_crosswalk` sits in `marts/vendor_b`), and `stg_telemetry__car_telemetry` has a sources YAML but no models YAML.
justifications.testing: Testing is layered well. Staging has key `unique`/`not_null`/`unique_combination_of_columns` tests in `_ergast__models.yml`. Every source column has format tests (`matches_pattern`) plus `no_conflicting_duplicates`/`no_redelivered_rows` in `_ergast__sources.yml`. Marts have `row_count_equals` grain guards and reconciliation tests (`assert_champions_match_reference`, `assert_pit_stop_mart_reconciles`, `assert_lap_times_match_source`). Unit tests in `_ergast__unit_tests.yml` rebuild the Ferrari trailing-space and race-1142 re-deliveries, so the ticket 5 and 6 bugs would be caught.
justifications.quirks: Every listed quirk is handled on purpose and documented. `clean_text` maps both `\N` and empty string to null. `lap_time_to_ms` parses strictly by regex. `max_pit_stop_ms` excludes red-flag stops. Standings come from the published tables, so pre-1991 drop scores, shared drives and sprint points are reproduced and reconciled against `reference_world_champions`. `int_seasons` stops incomplete 2024 from counting as a title. `int_driver_ids` creates placeholder rows for late-arriving drivers. The README 'Data quirks' section adds race 71 and Schumacher 1997.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: `fct_lap_times`/`fct_stints` use race-at-a-time `delete+insert` on `race_id`, so they handle lap renumbering, with a correction window (`lap_correction_window_races`) and a warn-level drift test that tells you when to full-refresh. `fct_telemetry` uses a `_LOADED_AT` watermark with a 6 h lookback and literal race lists so partitions are pruned. `snp_drivers.yml` uses check-all with `hard_deletes: invalidate`, which is right for a source with no `updated_at`. The weak spots: the lap window counts races rather than time, and `loaded_at = current_timestamp()` makes recent races rewrite on every run.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets refactored instead of bolting on. `dim_drivers.sql` was renamed to `dim_drivers_v2.sql`, and v1 is derived from v2 so the driver logic lives in one place. Vendor fixes were absorbed into `parse_date`/`dedupe` and logged in the README table. I found no TODOs, commented-out SQL or dead models. The only loose end is that the README and `scripts/ci.sh` depend on a committed `prod-artifacts/` that is gone from HEAD, removed by the final 'remove local config' commit, which may be the harness rather than the author.
justifications.docs: Model headers explain the reasoning: `fct_stints.sql` says when a race is recomputed, `int_pit_stops_enriched.sql` explains pit-lane time versus stationary time, and `parse_date` explains why AUTO detection is never used. The YAML descriptions call out grain caveats, such as `fct_results` noting pre-1979 two-car entries. The README covers layers, key definitions, the vendor-change log, telemetry cost measurements and when to full-refresh.
justifications.interfaces: `_groups.yml` defines an owned `f1_core` group with only `fct_results` and `dim_drivers` public and everything else protected by default (`dbt_project.yml`). Both have enforced contracts. `dim_drivers` v2 ships with a deprecation date on v1, v1 keeps its relation name and column order, and the README has a migration guide. The unit tests are named for behaviour (`dim_drivers_v1_keeps_full_name_contract`, `late_arriving_driver_gets_placeholder_with_career_stats`).
justifications.open_ended: `docs/leadership_answers.md` and `mart_driver_car_overperformance.sql` measure same-session qualifying gaps to the teammate, adjust for each teammate's strength against their other teammates, and give 95% intervals and rankability thresholds. They also explain why raw H2H misleads, using the Sainz example. For pit stops, `mart_pit_stop_trends.sql` adjusts for circuit and pushes back that the data holds pit-lane time, not stationary time, so it can't test the headline claim. Limitations and confounders are stated (the 2014 rule change, coverage starting in 2006, equal machinery assumed).

biggest_strength: Defensive handling of vendor changes is built into the project: the on-run-start schema guard (`check_source_schemas.sql`), format tests on every source column, dedupe plus conflicting-duplicate tests, and mart grain/reconciliation tests. Together they make the ticket 5/6 failure modes fail loudly before a mart is replaced, and each incident is recorded in the README log.
biggest_weakness: There is some duplicated logic and layer-skipping in the marts. `mart_constructor_season_pit_stops.sql` re-implements the service-stop filter and constructor join that `int_pit_stops_enriched.sql` already provides, and several marts join staging models directly. On top of that, the lap correction window counts races rather than using a time-based lookback and restamps `loaded_at` on every run, so the incremental models are not strictly idempotent.
